name: Caladh
long_description: Caladh protects critical maritime infrastructure from drone attacks above and below the waterline.  Our systems detect, track, and defeat unmanned systems so they can't get near the assets they want to disrupt.
one_liner: Anti-drone defense for the maritime domain

launches.title: Caladh: Anti-drone maritime defense
launches.tagline: Caladh protects critical maritime infrastructure from drone attacks above and below the waterline so they can't get near the assets they want to disrupt.
launches.body:
**TL;DR Underwater drones can navigate under the surface to reach ports, ships and seafloor cables, and no reliable solution exists to stop them. Caladh systems detect, track and defeat hostile drones by bringing the principles of electronic warfare underwater.** \
\
I’m [**Kristen Kita**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kristen-railey-kita-18388722/), founder of Caladh ("Call-luh"). I've spent the past decade working on this problem, starting with my PhD at MIT and most recently as a Principal Investigator for DARPA Sync. I started Caladh to close the gaps I've seen in how we protect critical infrastructure.\
\
<https://youtu.be/oQJC_hS07DQ>

\
**What we do**

* **Eclipse: deny the drone.** Eclipse is a moored buoy that persistently protects ports, terminals, offshore energy sites and cable landings. It listens passively, and when a threat appears it triggers automatically or on an operator’s command. It then denies the vehicle its navigation, comms and sensing both above and below the waterline, so the drone can’t find its target or report back. A towed version deploys from a small boat for expeditionary missions. It’s non-kinetic, unattended, and it plugs into existing C2 and layered defenses.
* **Cloak: hide the target.** Cloak sits low on the seabed next to cables, pipelines and other subsea assets. It defeats the imaging sonar and cameras that drones use to find and map those assets, so the asset blends back into the seafloor.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=126106&key=user_uploads/3880244/585d7584-ead6-4de2-a3f6-5a19fdf33e8f)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=126106&key=user_uploads/3880244/162d1022-921b-44c5-bda8-f1ca80cedba9)

**Why now**

A cheap drone can now threaten an asset worth hundreds of millions. In December 2025, Ukraine claimed it struck a Kilo-class submarine with an underwater drone. Above the surface, missile and drone attacks at Bab-el-Mandeb cut Suez Canal trade by about 50% in early 2024, and in October 2026 naval drones hit at least six merchant ships in the Black Sea.

The seafloor is just as exposed. The Nord Stream pipelines sabotage shows what one strike on seabed infrastructure can cost: the largest methane release on record. Underwater drones now give attackers a cheaper, harder-to-attribute way to reach the same kinds of targets: ports, offshore energy and subsea cables, none of which has a perimeter below the waterline.

**Why me**

I’ve worked on this problem for 10 years. My PhD at MIT was on detecting and tracking underwater drones with passive sonar. Across five DARPA underwater drone programs spanning navigation, sensing and autonomy, I learned exactly how these vehicles fail. I conceived the counter-UUV concept for DARPA Sync, led the DARPA study that shaped the new program, and served as the Principal Investigator, demonstrating new approaches to defeat underwater drones.

**Asks**

Introductions to:

* Port and terminal security leads
* Offshore oil, gas and wind security leads
* Subsea cable and pipeline operators
* Navy, Marine Corps expeditionary and Naval Special Warfare operators
* Advisors with Navy acquisition or submarine/NSW operational experience

Contact us at [founders@caladh.com](mailto:founders@caladh.com) or on [caladh.com](http://caladh.com) 

_Caladh is a Gaelic word for harbor, haven or safe landing place._
